items.title: Ramadan moves through the year on the lunar calendar
items.claim: Why does Ramadan fall in different seasons across years?

options.text: It is fixed each year by Islamic council

The Islamic (Hijri) calendar is purely lunar with no intercalation; its 12 months total around 354 days; Ramadan therefore shifts about 11 days earlier each Gregorian year, cycling through all seasons over around 33 years
It is fixed to August every year

items.reveal:
Most other religious calendars (Jewish, Hindu, Buddhist) are lunisolar — they add intercalary months to keep festivals in fixed seasons. The Islamic calendar deliberately rejects intercalation, based on Quran 9:36-37.

The Hijri year begins from Muhammad's emigration (hijra) from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE. The Hijri year 1446 began in July 2024.

In tropical countries Ramadan stays around 12-14 hours of fasting daylight; in high latitudes in summer it can exceed 20 hours, raising practical questions for which contemporary scholars give differing rulings.
items.why: Calendar choices have theological consequences. The Islamic refusal to align the lunar year with the seasons produces a religious experience that cycles through climates and seasons — different from Christianity or Judaism.

items.title: Kosher rules separate meat and dairy
items.claim: What are the main categories of kosher (kashrut) restrictions?

options.text: Permitted animals (mammals that chew cud and have cloven hooves; fish with fins and scales); ritual slaughter (shechita); separation of meat and dairy in cooking, eating and utensils; specific prohibitions including pork, shellfish, mixing milk and meat
Only meals at synagogue must be kosher

items.reveal:
The meat-dairy separation derives from three repetitions of 'You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk' (Exodus 23:19, 34:26; Deuteronomy 14:21). Rabbinic interpretation extended this to all mixing of meat and dairy.

Leviticus 11 and Deuteronomy 14 list permitted and forbidden animals. Pork and shellfish are the most widely known prohibitions; rabbit, camel and birds of prey are also forbidden.

Shechita is ritual slaughter by a trained shochet with a perfectly sharp knife in a single cut — designed to be quick and to drain blood. Some European countries (Sweden, Norway, Switzerland, Belgian regions) have banned shechita without prior stunning on animal welfare grounds.
items.why: Religious practice is often embodied — daily eating, household kitchens, separate dishes. Kashrut is one of the clearest cases of belief expressed through bodily and domestic practice.

items.title: The Christian Bible's contents were not fixed until centuries after Christ
items.claim: When was the New Testament canon — the 27 books — first listed in its current form?

options.text: By the apostles themselves, before 70 CE
At the Council of Nicaea in 325 CE
Athanasius's Easter letter of 367 CE is the first surviving list of exactly the 27 books; consensus formed gradually through the 4th-5th centuries
By Pope Damasus I at the Council of Trent in 1546

items.reveal:
Athanasius of Alexandria's 39th Festal Letter (367 CE) is the first surviving document listing the 27 NT books we have today. Regional councils (Hippo 393, Carthage 397) confirmed it. The Trent council (1546) made it formal Catholic dogma — partly in response to the Reformation.

Nicaea (325) dealt with the Arian controversy, not the canon — a common confusion popularised by Dan Brown's 'The Da Vinci Code'.

Gospels left out include Thomas, Mary, Peter and the Infancy Gospel of James. Some books that nearly made it (the Shepherd of Hermas, 1 Clement) didn't.
items.why: The 'received text' image of Scripture obscures a long, contested human process. Knowing the canon was assembled doesn't disprove faith — but it changes the questions you can ask.
